summary: A neighborhood store closes and people name different people to blame: the landlord, the owner, the city that owned the building.
realLife: When a neighborhood supermarket in Cleveland closed, a council member blamed the landlord: the lease was up and the rent had risen 50 percent over the last one. When a Kansas City supermarket closed, the city itself owned the property and had spent nearly $1 million in the past year to keep it open, so the closing was a city matter. When a Florida downtown lost businesses, residents blamed a sale of the building and officials said the city cannot step into private real estate deals.
